text.insert: The agreed scope model distinguishes shared standards from standards for one game. Composition is implemented: the global set lives at knowledge/global/sources/injectable/decomp_standards, each game keeps its own records under games/<id>/knowledge/sources/injectable/decomp_standards, and loaders read game first, then global (game family wins). Records still use global_standard_v1 and global_standard IDs. Scope is carried by the root a record is read from, not by a record field.

props.description: Agreed applicability model. Implemented by root composition (global root at knowledge/global plus the game root); not yet a field on standard records.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Shared applicability or one selected game.

fields.name: gameId
fields.description: Required only when kind is game; identifies the registered game.

props.name: StandardScope — Proposed

text.insert: The intended effective set is shared standards plus the selected game's standards. Worker prompts, librarian recognition context, dashboard previews, and QA enforcement must use the same resolved set. Adding a field without updating these consumers would leave scope unenforced.

Whether a game-specific standard may override a global rule is unresolved. Do not infer override behavior from file order or duplicate IDs. Scope, conflict handling, and migration of existing standards need implementation and validation before onboarding can rely on them.
